set.n: Copper box of gold coins in a creek bank, Springdale township near Walnut Grove
set.pl: Creek reach in the N½ of the SW¼ of sec. 11 T109N R39W (Springdale township), on the farm as drawn in the 1930 Webb atlas of Redwood County (about 300 m). This is about 3 miles NW of Walnut Grove, not SW as the reprint says; all of the family's land lay NW of town, so the plat wins.
set.st: A farmer digging along a small creek bank on his farm found a watertight copper box, smaller than a brick, holding twelve $20 and one $10 gold pieces ($250). The AP (26 May 1930) said the coins were dated 1846-1853 and were believed buried during the 1862 Dakota War, and that a large tree near the spot had evidently served as a marker. Who buried it was never learned. Pin: Creek reach in the N½ of the SW¼ of sec. 11 T109N R39W (Springdale township), on the farm as drawn in the 1930 Webb atlas of Redwood County (about 300 m). This is about 3 miles NW of Walnut Grove, not SW as the reprint says; all of the family's land lay NW of town, so the plat wins.
src: AP, Walnut Grove, 26 May 1930: Albert Lea Tribune, 26 May 1930, p. 1 (newspapers.com image 1024136648); also Austin Daily Herald, St. Cloud Times, Winona Daily News
Sauk Centre Herald, 26 Jun 1930, p. 8, 'Excited Over Finding Gold', reprinted from the Tracy Headlight Herald (newspapers.com image 879918517, PC read)

set.t: Found, but whoever buried a copper box by a marker tree may have left more along the same creek bank. Check the creek through the SW¼ of sec. 11 on the 1938 aerial for an old large tree, then detect the bank with permission. Access: Private farmland: ask permission.
pinev: Farm placed on the 1930 Webb plat; creek crossing per NHDPlus. Two independent texts (AP and the Tracy reprint).
